calibration.note: Strongly anisotropic: 1 px = 28.96 nm in x, 1.116 nm in y. The figure is a laterally stretched view of a 120 um x 4 um window.

topology_reasoning.what_it_is: A subwavelength-grating (SWG) metamaterial 'multi-box' directional coupler. Everything visible sits on a single uniform lateral lattice of pitch p = 100.4 nm running along the propagation direction x; each lattice site is either an isolated narrow silicon strip (w = 65 nm, gap = 35 nm) or part of a solid rail formed by filling five consecutive sites.

measured_lattice.lattice_indices_present: k = -12 .. +12 (25 sites), symmetric about the device axis

site_assignment.|k| <= 2: 5 isolated strips = the shared SWG metamaterial gap region between the two arms (runs straight the full 120 um)
site_assignment.3 <= |k| <= 7: 5 sites filled solid = the guiding rail (bus) of each arm; measured width 0.467 um = 4*pitch + strip_width, exactly the merged-5-site width
site_assignment.8 <= |k| <= 12: 5 isolated strips = the outer SWG multi-box cladding of each arm

topology_reasoning.how_it_works: Each arm is a strip waveguide whose evanescent field is engineered by a lateral subwavelength array: the outer 5-strip multi-box cladding lowers the effective lateral index step and delocalizes the mode, while the 5-strip array in the shared gap acts as an anisotropic metamaterial bridge between the two arms. Because the strip pitch (100 nm) is far below lambda/2n, the array does not diffract; it behaves as a homogeneous uniaxial medium whose index is set by the duty cycle w/p. Power transfers between the two rails over the straight interaction length; the metamaterial gap raises and flattens the supermode index splitting versus wavelength, which is what buys the broadband / dispersion-engineered coupling that a plain two-strip coupler cannot get. The central gap array is left uncut across the whole frame (it continues beyond the crop) while the two arms fan away at both ends.

measured_longitudinal_layout.fan_behaviour: At both ends the arm (rail + its 5 cladding strips) curves away from the axis and leaves the 4 um window. The elements do NOT translate rigidly: each bends on its own radius, the outermost cladding strip most sharply. Fitting circular arcs to the edges gives R ~ 9.7 um for the rail (k=5) and R ~ 3.5 um for the outermost strip (k=12), i.e. curvature increasing roughly linearly with lattice index: 1/R = b*(k - k0). This is a fan-out that separates the array elements as they leave the coupling region.
measured_longitudinal_layout.verification: Predicted exit points (where an element crosses the top of the 4 um window) : rail at x ~ 4.6 um, outermost strip at x ~ 7.6 um. Measured in the image: rail leaves at x ~ 4.5 um, outermost strip at x ~ 7.6 um.

function_defining_knobs: pitch_um - sets the metamaterial regime (must stay << lambda/2n_eff) and, with strip_width_um, the duty cycle
strip_width_um - duty cycle -> equivalent metamaterial index of both the cladding and the gap
n_gap_strips - number of SWG strips bridging the two arms; the dominant coupling-strength knob
n_bus_sites - solid rail width (= n_bus_sites*pitch - gap); sets the arm's own mode confinement
n_clad_strips - outer multi-box cladding depth; sets lateral delocalisation / dispersion engineering
coupling_length_um - straight interaction length; sets the transfer ratio for a given coupling strength
bend_curvature_per_period / bend_curvature_zero_index - the fan-out law that takes the arms out of the coupling region
topology_reasoning.primitives_used: gf.Path centerlines (straight + circular arc segments computed analytically) extruded at constant width on layer (1,0); no gf.components stencils, no raw polygons.

iterations.change_made: First model: single lateral lattice (pitch 0.1004 um, strip 0.066 um after the 2-dbu snap), 5 sites merged into each rail (0.468 um), rails+cladding fanned out on circular arcs with curvature 1/R = 0.0261*(k-1.09); gap array straight across 0-120 um.

Strip width 0.066 -> 0.068 um (rendered strips were ~2 px thin); fan curvature scaled down 15% (arcs were over-bent); gap array offset -0.0052 um and top-arm fan exit biased +0.0029 um to register the pattern to the frame (the source figure is not exactly mirror symmetric).
Refit the fan curvature law from the rendered-vs-target bend edges: 1/R = 0.0257*(k-1.305) (rail R~10.5 um, outermost cladding strip R~3.6 um).

Diagnosed the dominant residual: in the target the cladding strips WIDEN and merge into a solid access waveguide as the arm leaves the coupling region (measured 0.065 -> 0.096 -> merged over ~0.8 um). Added the multi-box -> strip transition as a width taper along each fan-out arc (rate 0.045 um per um of arc length, capped at 0.22 um), discretised into 48 constant-width extrusions.
REGRESSION (rejected): narrowed the gap-array duty cycle to 0.066 um and re-tilted the curvature law to 0.02276*(k-0.531). Precision rose 0.983->0.986 but recall fell 0.984->0.979; net IoU -0.0027.

Reverted iteration 5 to the measured best; added lengths.json (path lengths computed from the extruded gf.Path point arrays) and flattened the top cell before write_gds so gdstk top_level() sees the polygons. IoU identical to iteration 4 to 5 decimal places.

knob_verification.width_um_justification: cross-section that scales with the length knob = 2 rails x 0.470 um + 10 cladding strips x 0.068 um = 1.620 um (the gap array is fixed to the 120 um window and does not scale with it).
knob_verification.reading: area_ok TRUE: perturbing coupling_length_um by +5 um grew the layer-(1,0) polygon area by 8.1000 um^2 against an expected 8.1000 um^2 -- the knob moves real geometry. delta_length_ok is FALSE BY CONSTRUCTION and is not a defect: that half of the check is the MZI contract (arm imbalance), and this device is a symmetric coupler whose two arms are mirror images, so delta_length_um is exactly 0. lengths.json reports it honestly as 0 rather than being contorted to make an MZI assertion pass.
knob_verification.additional_reading: pitch_um, strip_width_um, n_gap_strips, n_clad_strips and bus_merge_rate_per_um each move the layer-(1,0) area by 3.9-30.2 um^2 when perturbed -- every declared function knob drives geometry.

honest_limitations: Residual error is split roughly half in the fan-out regions (x<11 um and x>103 um) and half in the straight section.

In the straight section the residual is quantisation-bound: kfactory requires extrusion widths on a 0.002 um grid and the raster resolves 0.00112 um per pixel, so a target strip of 0.0647 um can only be drawn as 0.066 or 0.068 um; 0.068 was kept because it balances precision against recall. The target's own gap-array strips are not uniform (0.058-0.068 um in the figure), which a single duty-cycle knob cannot and should not chase.
In the fan-out the width taper is modelled as linear in arc length with a cap; the source figure's merge is slightly faster near the bend start and keeps widening further out than the cap allows.
The 120 x 4 um window is a crop: the arms and the gap array both continue beyond it, so the fan-out arcs are drawn until they clear the frame rather than terminating on a port.
